children: have turned down a proposal from Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO) that would have required the chipmakers to put up a combined 25T won ($18.7B) in advance to help fund power infrastructure for their planned semiconductor clusters,
would have paid about 20T won, while SK Hynix
would have contributed roughly 5T won. The money was intended to help speed up the development of electricity infrastructure needed to support the companies’ expanding chip operations.

The companies were unsure whether such large upfront payments were necessary, given uncertainty over the long-term durability of semiconductor demand, a company official said, according to the report.
South Korea faces rising power demand from semiconductor manufacturing and AI infrastructure. The rejection leaves KEPCO to seek other ways to fund the required power infrastructure.
